statement.text:
Let G be a finite group, B a block of characters of G, D(B) its defect group
and k(B) (respectively, k0 (B)) the number of all irreducible complex characters (of
height 0) lying in B. Conjectures:
    a) (R. Brauer) k(B) ⩽ |D(B)|; this has been proved for p-soluble groups
(D. Gluck, K. Magaard, U. Riese, P. Schmid, J. Algebra, 279 (2004), 694–719);
    b) (J. B. Olsson) k0 (B) ⩽ |D(B) : D(B)′ |, where D(B)′ is the derived subgroup
of D(B);
    c) (R. Brauer) D(B) is abelian if and only if k0 (B) = k(B).      V. D. Mazurov
